provenance.note: `Notifications` takes a whole `SignifyClient`, so the real client is driven with `globalThis.fetch` replaced by a recorder that signs its answers as a KERIA agent would and can set a `Content-Range`. The clock and the agent's key are pinned, and the sample nonce is built from fixed bytes by the reference's own `Matter` under the code `randomNonce` uses. `PUBLIC TEST MATERIAL`: the passcode is the pinned tests' own and has never protected anything; the nonce is derived from a counting pattern and identifies nothing.

declarations.list_return: return { start: range.start, end: range.end, total: range.total, notes: notes, };
declarations.notification_type: Notification: { i: string; dt: string; r: boolean; a: components['schemas']['NotificationData']; };

notification_identifier.documentation: /** * Mark a notification as read * @async * @param {string} said SAID of the notification * @returns {Promise<string>} A promise to the result of the marking */
notification_identifier.signify_random_nonce: export function randomNonce(): string { const seed = libsodium.randombytes_buf(libsodium.crypto_sign_SEEDBYTES); const seedqb64 = new Matter({ raw: seed, code: MtrDex.Ed25519_Seed }); return seedqb64.qb64; }
notification_identifier.note: `mark(said)` and `delete(said)` name the parameter `said` and the JSDoc says "SAID of the notification". It is not one: keripy's `notice()` builds the record with `i=""` and its `Dicter` fills an empty identifier with `randomNonce()`. The two references disagree about that nonce's code — signify-ts's `randomNonce` uses the Ed25519 seed code `A` over thirty-two bytes, keripy's the 128-bit salt code `0A` over sixteen — and **neither is a digest code**, so the field is not a SAID under either. KERIA is built on keripy, so what a real agent writes is the `0A` form.
notification_identifier.rust_decision: the argument is **not** typed as Roadmap 3.3's `Said`, which would refuse every identifier a real agent produces. It stays borrowed text encoded exactly once by Roadmap 5.3's builder — the shape Roadmap 6.5 gave an operation name — which is enough to close the path injection this fixture records. keripy is corroboration for what fills the field, not a governing reference (ADR `0009`).

pinned_confirmations.note: the pinned case asserts all three paths, all three methods, and the `Range` header exactly. What it does **not** provide is a real notification identifier: its literal is the string `notificationSAID`, and every integration call site passes a runtime `note.i` read back from a live agent — so the shape of that field is established from `randomNonce` and keripy rather than from any pinned literal.

the_window_defaults_are_observable.note: `list(start = 0, end = 24)` writes both defaults into the `Range` header, so an omitted window is still a request that names one
the_window_defaults_are_observable.rust_decision: the window is a required `ItemRange` and `DEFAULT_WINDOW` names the reference's values, so what is asked for is visible at the call site — Roadmap 6.6's identifier listing already takes its window the same way

a_window_bound_is_not_an_integer.note: both bounds are `number` and reach the header through template interpolation, so `list(1.5, 2.5)` sends `notes=1.5-2.5` and `list(40, 20)` sends a window whose end precedes its start
a_window_bound_is_not_an_integer.rust_decision: **refused**: Roadmap 5.3's `ItemRange` takes two `u64` and validates that the start does not exceed the end, so neither is representable. A fraction is not a count of items and a reversed window asks for nothing.

an_absent_content_range_becomes_three_ze.note: `parseRangeHeaders(null, 'notes')` returns `{start: 0, end: 0, total: 0}`, so a page of real notifications is reported as an empty window rather than as an unknown one
an_absent_content_range_becomes_three_ze.rust_decision: reproduced as Roadmap 5.3 already decided and Roadmap 6.6 already applied: the window is an `Option`, so an unreported one is `None` and stays distinguishable from a genuinely empty one

the_identifier_is_not_encoded.note: both single-notification paths are `'/notifications/' + said`, so a value carrying `?` turns the path into a query — Roadmap 5.3's own fixture recorded `notifications().mark('a?b=c')` doing exactly that, and Roadmap 3.10 signs `@path`
the_identifier_is_not_encoded.rust_decision: closed by Roadmap 5.3's builder, which encodes every path component exactly once and offers no way to skip it

mark_returns_its_body_as_text.note: `mark` is the only method here that reads its answer, and it reads it with `res.text()` — which replaces any byte that is not valid UTF-8 with U+FFFD rather than failing
mark_returns_its_body_as_text.rust_decision: the text is returned, because the reference genuinely offers it, but decoded **strictly**: a body that is not valid UTF-8 is `ClientError::Decode` where `res.text()` silently repairs it. That is the decision Roadmap 6.11 made for a CESR answer read the same way.

a_delete_carries_no_body.note: `delete` passes `undefined` where `list` and `mark` pass `null`, so the request carries no body at all
a_delete_carries_no_body.rust_decision: reproduced: no body is set on the request, as Roadmap 6.5's, 7.3's, and 7.4's deletes already do

the_page_is_never_typed.declaration: return { start: range.start, end: range.end, total: range.total, notes: notes, };
the_page_is_never_typed.note: `list` returns `Promise<any>` and its `notes` field is `await res.json()` with no cast at all — not even the compile-time claim the other families make
the_page_is_never_typed.rust_decision: decoded into `signify_types::api::Notification`, so an entry missing the fields the schema declares is refused; the recorded wrong-shaped page is proven refused

the_window_is_returned_flattened.declaration: return { start: range.start, end: range.end, total: range.total, notes: notes, };
the_window_is_returned_flattened.note: the three window numbers are spread into the returned object beside `notes`, so a caller cannot tell the window apart from the page
the_window_is_returned_flattened.rust_decision: `NotificationListing` keeps them apart — an optional `window` and the notifications — which is the shape Roadmap 6.6 gave the identifier listing for the same reason
